q: Under day-work (time-rate) payment, costing of jobs depends heavily on time booking, for the reason that:

options.A: Wages under day-work are not paid at all unless a job is completed
options.B: The wages paid for attendance have no direct relation to output, so the cost of a job can be known only by distributing the time wages over the jobs on which time was booked
options.C: Output under day-work is automatically measured by the pay sheet
options.D: Piece rates for every job are fixed under day-work

q: The cost sheet of a batch order in a workshop differs from that of a job order in that the batch cost sheet shows:

options.A: The cost of one single article ordered by a customer
options.B: Only the material cost of the batch, labour and on-cost being excluded
options.C: The total cost of the whole lot produced under the batch order, from which the cost per article of the lot is derived
options.D: The wages of the shop for one day only

q: Under the railway classification of Plan Heads, Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is operated as:

options.A: Plan Head 71 - Stores Suspense
options.B: Plan Head 73 - Miscellaneous Advances
options.C: Plan Head 32 - Track Renewals
options.D: Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense

q: Workshop staff earn a night shift allowance that cannot be linked to any individual job. In workshop costing, such an allowance is treated as:

options.A: A direct charge on the jobs worked during the night shift
options.B: Part of on-cost (overhead)
options.C: Proforma on-cost
options.D: A recovery from the staff concerned

q: Articles manufactured in a workshop for another railway have to be packed and despatched to that railway. The cost of such packing and despatch is:

options.A: Borne as general on-cost of the workshop
options.B: Recovered from the stores depot
options.C: Written off as a loss of the workshop
options.D: Charged to the work order (job) concerned

q: In workshop accounts, the abbreviation 'WGR' stands for:

options.A: Workshop Goods Register
options.B: Workshop General Register
options.C: Wages and Gratuity Register
options.D: Workshop Gate Register

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'WAMS', used in connection with workshops, stands for:

options.A: Workshop Accounts Management System
options.B: Workshop Asset Maintenance Schedule
options.C: Wages and Materials System
options.D: Workshop Administration and Manning Scheme

q: A stores requisition from a shop of a workshop is headed 'T&P'. In this context, 'T&P' refers to:

options.A: Trains and Parcels
options.B: Time and Productivity
options.C: Transfer and Posting
options.D: Tools and Plant

q: Machinery and plant for workshops and production units are procured centrally through an organisation set up for the modernisation of workshops. That organisation, COFMOW, is primarily engaged in:

options.A: Centralised procurement of machinery and plant for workshops and production units
options.B: Periodic overhaul of locomotives and coaches
options.C: Audit of the accounts of railway workshops
options.D: Manufacture of wheels and axles for rolling stock

q: A Workshop Accounts Officer needs the codal provisions governing the working and accounts of his workshop. He should refer to:

options.A: The Indian Railway Code for the Rolling Stock Department (Rolling Stock Code)
options.B: The Indian Railway Stores Code
options.C: The Indian Railway Traffic (Commercial) Code
options.D: The General Financial Rules

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a production workshop of Indian Railways from a repair workshop?

options.A: A production workshop carries out only Periodic Overhaul of coaches
options.B: A repair workshop manufactures new locomotives, coaches and wagons
options.C: A production workshop manufactures new rolling stock such as locomotives, coaches and wagons, whereas a repair workshop overhauls and repairs existing stock
options.D: A repair workshop does not maintain any accounts of its jobs

q: According to the nature of rolling stock dealt with, the workshops of Indian Railways fall broadly into the three classes of:

options.A: Government workshops, private workshops and departmental workshops
options.B: Day workshops, night workshops and combined workshops
options.C: Audited workshops, unaudited workshops and departmental workshops
options.D: Locomotive workshops, carriage and wagon workshops, and combined workshops

q: The shops within a large workshop — machine shop, smithy, foundry, erecting shop and the like — are set up on the basis of:

options.A: Seniority of the staff posted in them
options.B: Trade or process
options.C: Age of the buildings in which they are housed
options.D: Names of the shop incharges

q: A machine in the machine shop breaks down and a new machine has to be installed in its place. The installation, maintenance and repair of the workshop's machinery and plant is primarily the responsibility of the:

options.A: Pattern shop
options.B: Paint shop
options.C: Millwright shop
options.D: Upholstery shop

q: Components are being manufactured in a workshop against a sanctioned capital work, but are not yet complete. Until they are completed and their cost is transferred to the head of the capital work concerned, the cost accumulated on them remains under:

options.A: Stores Suspense
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Shop on-cost
options.D: Revenue working expenses

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are carried forward from year to year without any verification of the jobs in progress.
2. At the close of the financial year, the balances under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are verified with the jobs actually in progress, so that the balance carried forward represents genuine work-in-progress.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The estimates framed under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense cannot be framed in isolation; they are necessarily linked with the Stores Budget and the Revenue Demands. This linkage arises because:

options.A: Stores purchases for the whole railway are made by the workshop itself
options.B: Revenue demands are sanctioned by the Workshop Accounts Officer
options.C: The workshop prepares the budget of the entire railway
options.D: The workshop's outturn is transferred partly to stores stock and partly to revenue repair heads

q: In a production unit turning out locomotives, the Accounts office is required to compile the cost of manufacture:

options.A: For all the units turned out in a year together, in one lump sum
options.B: At the prevailing market price of a similar unit
options.C: Unit-wise, for each individual unit turned out, comprising material, labour and on-cost including proforma charges
options.D: On the basis of material cost only, unit-wise

q: A locomotive is built in a workshop by combining foundry castings, machined components and final erection. Costing of such manufacture, which combines several methods of costing, is known as:

options.A: Process costing alone
options.B: Batch costing alone
options.C: Operating costing
options.D: Multiple (composite) costing

q: Batch costing, as applied to standard components manufactured in lots for stocking in a workshop, is a variant of:

options.A: Process costing
options.B: Operating costing
options.C: Job costing
options.D: Marginal costing

q: Foremen and chargemen of a shop supervise the work of the shop generally; their time is not booked to any individual job. Their salaries are therefore charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: The first job taken up each day
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as direct labour

q: A chargeman spends the whole of his time for a month supervising one single large manufacture job, to the exclusion of all other work. His pay for that month is treated as:

options.A: Shop on-cost of his shop
options.B: General on-cost of the workshop
options.C: A direct charge on that job
options.D: Proforma on-cost

q: Inspectors and testing staff of a workshop examine the outturn of the shops but are not themselves booked to individual jobs. The cost of such inspection and testing is treated as:

options.A: A direct charge on each article inspected
options.B: An item of on-cost of the shop/workshop
options.C: A recovery from the stores depot
options.D: A charge to the Capital head

q: A workshop's drawing and design office prepares designs for the workshop as a whole and not for one shop alone. Its expenses form part of:

options.A: Shop on-cost of the erecting shop only
options.B: The cost of the first job designed
options.C: Stores Suspense
options.D: General on-cost of the workshop

q: Safety helmets, gloves and other protective clothing are supplied to shop staff for use on their work. The cost of such clothing and equipment is charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: The individual jobs on which the staff happen to be working
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: The personal accounts of the staff concerned

q: Files, hammers and similar small hand tools of a consumable nature are issued to a shop for general use. In workshop costing, their cost is treated as:

options.A: Capitalised as tools and plant
options.B: Charged in full to the first job on which they are used
options.C: Consumable stores, their cost being charged to shop on-cost
options.D: Recovered from the workers using them

q: A crane installed in a workshop works solely for one shop, lifting material for that shop alone. The cost of working that crane is charged to:

options.A: The general on-cost of the whole workshop
options.B: The shop on-cost of the shop served
options.C: The jobs on which the crane happens to lift material
options.D: The capital account of the workshop

q: An ambulance room and medical facilities are maintained in a workshop for the benefit of its staff. The cost of maintaining them is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on jobs
options.B: Proforma on-cost
options.C: Deducted from the wages of workers
options.D: General on-cost (welfare overhead)

q: A workshop has no separate power meters for its shops. Its total power bill must nevertheless be apportioned among the shops, and this is generally done on the basis of:

options.A: The connected load (total horse power/kilowatts of the machines installed) of each shop
options.B: The number of workers employed in each shop
options.C: The floor area occupied by each shop
options.D: The value of outturn of each shop

q: Power is consumed in a workshop for lighting the premises generally; no particular shop can be identified with this consumption. Such power cost is charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost of the largest shop
options.B: The jobs under execution during night hours
options.C: General on-cost of the workshop
options.D: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

q: The electrical shop of a workshop carries out repairs to a machine belonging to the machine shop, the work being booked on a work order. Although the electrical shop executed the work, the cost is ultimately borne:

options.A: By the executing shop, as the cost of its own jobs
options.B: By debit to Capital, in all cases
options.C: By the stores depot which supplied the material
options.D: By the shop owning the machine, as part of its on-cost

q: For several periods, the on-cost actually incurred in a workshop has persistently differed widely from the on-cost absorbed on its jobs at the rates in force. In such a situation, the rates in force are required to be:

options.A: Left unchanged
options.B: Revised
options.C: Doubled
options.D: Abolished altogether

q: Job costs in a workshop cannot be completed until the shop's on-cost has been charged to the individual jobs done in it. This process of charging on-cost to jobs is known as:

options.A: Allocation of on-cost
options.B: Apportionment of on-cost
options.C: Absorption of on-cost
options.D: Accumulation of on-cost

q: A workshop does not wait for the actual indirect expenses of a month to be collected before costing its jobs; it charges on-cost at predetermined rates. This practice is followed mainly so that:

options.A: Job costs can be compiled and the outturn transferred promptly, without waiting for the actual indirect expenses of the period to be collected
options.B: The actual on-cost need never be ascertained
options.C: The shops can fix their own rates without any basis
options.D: On-cost can be charged at double the actual amount

q: In a shop where work is done almost entirely by hand and machines play an insignificant part, the most suitable basis for absorbing on-cost on jobs is:

options.A: The material cost of the jobs
options.B: The number of articles produced in the shop
options.C: The floor area occupied by each job
options.D: Direct labour hours worked on the jobs (labour-hour rate)

q: The cost sheet of a workshop job includes direct material, direct labour, shop and general on-cost and proforma on-cost. Which of the following does it NOT include?

options.A: Direct material consumed on the job
options.B: Interest on the capital invested in the workshop
options.C: Proforma on-cost, i.e., Provident Fund contribution and depreciation
options.D: Shop on-cost and general on-cost

q: After castings are taken out of the moulds in a foundry, runners, risers and adhering sand are removed from them and they are cleaned. This operation is known as:

options.A: Fettling
options.B: Melting
options.C: Moulding
options.D: Painting

q: A workshop requires additional covered accommodation and an extension to one of its shop buildings is constructed. The cost of this construction is charged:

options.A: To Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: To shop on-cost of the shop housed in the building
options.C: To Capital/Depreciation Reserve Fund through a works estimate
options.D: To a revenue standing work order

q: A component required for a specific job is got fabricated through an outside agency, which raises its bill on the workshop. In compiling the cost of the job, the agency's bill is:

options.A: Charged to shop on-cost
options.B: Charged to general on-cost
options.C: Ignored in the cost of the job
options.D: Charged to that job as a direct expense

q: Material is purchased specially for one particular job and freight and carriage are paid on bringing it to the workshop. This freight and carriage is:

options.A: Charged to general on-cost of the workshop
options.B: Charged to that job as a direct expense, forming part of its prime cost
options.C: Charged to the stores depot as its handling expense
options.D: Recovered from the supplier in all cases

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The overtime premium, i.e., the extra amount paid over the normal rate for overtime hours, is ordinarily charged to shop on-cost.
2. Where overtime is worked specifically on a job in order to meet an urgent requirement of the customer (indentor), the overtime premium is charged to that job itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A premium bonus plan pays a worker bonus on a graduated scale related to his efficiency, the bonus beginning at a prescribed minimum level of efficiency, commonly 66-2/3 per cent. This plan is known as:

options.A: Emerson's efficiency plan
options.B: Taylor's differential piece-rate system
options.C: The Halsey plan
options.D: The Rowan plan

q: Under one of the premium bonus plans, the worker receives, as bonus, 30 per cent of the value of the time saved by him. That plan is the:

options.A: Halsey plan
options.B: Halsey-Weir plan
options.C: Rowan plan
options.D: Bedaux plan

q: In a system of wage payment, work is measured in 'points' or B units, one point representing one minute of work at standard performance, including a proportion for rest. That system is the:

options.A: Gantt system
options.B: Merrick system
options.C: Bedaux system
options.D: Emerson system

q: A wage plan guarantees a worker his day wages and, in addition, pays him a bonus when he completes the standard task set for him. This plan is known as:

options.A: Halsey plan
options.B: Rowan plan
options.C: Taylor's differential piece-rate system
options.D: Gantt's task and bonus plan

q: A worker attends to several machines at the same time, and machines sometimes wait for his attention. The allowance added to the allowed time to cover such waiting of machines is called:

options.A: Fatigue allowance
options.B: Interference allowance
options.C: Contingency allowance
options.D: Policy allowance

q: A machine is set up once for a batch of components. In fixing the allowed time per piece for the batch, the setting-up time is taken into account by:

options.A: Spreading it over the whole batch, i.e., adding the setting-up time divided by the batch quantity to the per-piece time
options.B: Charging it wholly to the first piece of the batch
options.C: Ignoring it altogether, as it is not productive time
options.D: Treating it as idle time of the operator

q: The incentive scheme in a workshop covers direct workers on measured jobs, gang workers and essential indirect workers attached to the shops. It does NOT cover:

options.A: Direct workers engaged on measured jobs
options.B: Gang workers sharing the bonus of their group
options.C: Essential indirect workers attached to the shops
options.D: General indirect and office (clerical) staff not connected with production

q:
Consider the following statements about revision of allowed times under the incentive scheme:
1. An allowed time must be revised if the method of working, the machine used or the material worked on changes.
2. Management may cut an allowed time at any time merely in order to step up the outturn of the shop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Which of the following correctly describes the charge fed into a foundry cupola?

options.A: Finished castings and moulding sand
options.B: New steel billets only
options.C: Pig iron, foundry returns/scrap and coke as fuel, together with flux as required
options.D: Coal tar and lubricating oil only

q: A locomotive has failed in service and is sent to the workshop for emergent repairs so that it can be put back into service. In maintenance terminology, work of this kind is classified as:

options.A: Mid-Life Rehabilitation of the locomotive
options.B: Preventive maintenance, being attention given before any failure
options.C: Periodic Overhaul of the locomotive
options.D: Corrective maintenance, being repair carried out after a failure has occurred

q: In the maintenance of workshop machinery, predictive maintenance is best described as maintenance which is:

options.A: Carried out only after a machine has broken down and stopped production
options.B: Carried out on all machines at fixed intervals laid down in a schedule, whether they need it or not
options.C: Planned from the monitored condition of the machine, attention being given when measurements such as vibration show deterioration, before a breakdown occurs
options.D: Carried out by the machine operators themselves as part of their daily cleaning duties

q: Replacement of a machine in a workshop under the Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme is generally justified on:

options.A: The age-cum-condition basis, the age of the machine and its present condition being taken together
options.B: Age alone, every machine being replaced at a fixed age in all cases
options.C: Breakdown alone, a machine being replaced only after it has finally broken down
options.D: The recommendation of the machine manufacturer alone

q: Provision for the machinery and plant required for workshops is made under:

options.A: Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock
options.B: Plan Head 41 - Machinery and Plant
options.C: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, as a suspense head
options.D: The Rolling Stock Programme head for locomotives and coaches

q: A machine in a workshop is said to have become obsolete when:

options.A: It is worn out by constant use and can no longer be run at all
options.B: Improved designs or methods have made it out of date and it has lost its usefulness and value, although it may still be physically serviceable
options.C: It is damaged in an accident and has to be repaired before use
options.D: It is kept idle for want of work in the shop for a short period

q: Material or a finished article is allowed to be taken out of the premises of a railway workshop only:

options.A: On the verbal permission of the chargeman of the shop
options.B: Under a gate pass issued by the competent authority
options.C: Against a personal surety of the worker carrying it
options.D: After the close of the financial year

q: Under VED analysis, as applied to the material held for workshop use, items are classified according to:

options.A: The value of the annual consumption of each item
options.B: The unit price of each item, from the highest to the lowest
options.C: The criticality of each item for production, that is, the effect on production if the item is not available when required
options.D: The speed at which each item is consumed in the shops

q: Under HML analysis, as applied to the material held for workshop use, items are classified according to:

options.A: The rate at which the items are consumed in the workshop
options.B: The criticality of the items for the working of the workshop
options.C: The total annual value of the consumption of the items
options.D: The unit price of the items, the items being grouped as high, medium and low in unit price

q: In the stores control of workshop material, the stock of an item has fallen to the level at which a fresh purchase order must be placed so that the new supply arrives before the existing stock runs out. This level is known as:

options.A: The danger level
options.B: The re-order level
options.C: The maximum level
options.D: The minimum level

q: Stock of an item held in reserve over and above the quantity expected to be used, so that production is guarded against delayed supplies or a sudden rise in demand, is known as:

options.A: Safety stock
options.B: Surplus stock
options.C: Dead surplus stock
options.D: Work-in-progress stock

q: A shop needs small quantities of consumable stores every day. Instead of drawing them from the main stores depot on each occasion, such stores are generally held:

options.A: In the personal custody of the chargeman, without any accountal
options.B: In the cash office of the workshop
options.C: Only in the main stores depot, shops not being allowed to hold any stores
options.D: In the shop itself under an imprest arrangement, replenished from the stores depot as the stores are consumed

q: Routine Overhaul (ROH) of wagons differs from their Periodic Overhaul in respect of the place where it is carried out, namely:

options.A: Only in production units
options.B: Only at the workshops of the Railway Board
options.C: In wagon depots (sick lines), and not in workshops
options.D: At the stations where the wagons are loaded

q: Axles of rolling stock under Periodic Overhaul in a workshop are examined by ultrasonic testing. The object of this test is primarily to:

options.A: Measure the diameter of the axle journal
options.B: Check the profile of the wheel tyre
options.C: Determine the age of the axle
options.D: Detect internal cracks and flaws not visible on the surface

q: In a repair workshop, all the material needed for the Periodic Overhaul of a coach is assembled in advance as a single set, ready to be issued to the job when the coach is taken in hand. This advance assembly of POH material is called:

options.A: Kitting of POH material
options.B: Batching of outturn
options.C: Pooling of stores
options.D: Loading of machines

q: In fixing the economic batch quantity for batch manufacture in a workshop, two opposing costs are balanced against each other, namely:

options.A: The material cost and the labour cost of the batch
options.B: The fixed cost and the variable cost of the workshop
options.C: The setting-up (preparation) cost of the batch and the cost of carrying or holding the stock produced
options.D: The cost of inspection and the cost of transport of the batch

q: The wages of the machine operator are included in one type of machine-hour rate, over and above the expenses of running the machine. That rate is called the:

options.A: Ordinary machine-hour rate
options.B: Comprehensive machine-hour rate
options.C: Standing machine-hour rate
options.D: Simple machine-hour rate

q: Rent, rates and taxes of the workshop premises form a common charge of the workshop. Among the shops, this charge is generally apportioned on the basis of:

options.A: The floor area occupied by each shop
options.B: The direct wages booked in each shop
options.C: The number of workers employed in each shop
options.D: The machine hours worked in each shop

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'scrap' from 'waste' in costing terminology?

options.A: Waste has a sale value, whereas scrap has no value
options.B: Scrap has a realisable (sale) value, whereas waste, such as loss by evaporation or shrinkage, has no value
options.C: Scrap and waste mean one and the same thing
options.D: Scrap is a finished product, whereas waste is a raw material

q: The cost of converting material into the finished article on a workshop job, excluding the material cost itself, that is, its direct labour and the on-cost charged on it, is termed the:

options.A: Direct material cost of the job
options.B: Conversion cost of the job
options.C: Full cost of the job including proforma on-cost
options.D: Departmental charges leviable on the job

q: Although nuts, bolts and washers issued in bulk to a shop are used on identifiable jobs, they are not booked job-wise. The costing practice behind this treatment is that:

options.A: Such material is a free gift of the stores depot
options.B: Material of very small value is treated as a consumable charge to on-cost for convenience, the cost and effort of booking it to each job being out of proportion to its value
options.C: Such material is charged to the first job of the month in full
options.D: Such material is recovered from the workers using it

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fixing on-cost rates with reference to normal capacity working protects job costs from distortion by purely temporary fluctuations in the volume of outturn.
2. On-cost rates are refixed every month on the basis of that month's actual hours alone.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A semi-variable overhead item changes with the volume of outturn, though not in direct proportion to it, being partly fixed and partly variable in behaviour.
2. When the outturn of a shop falls to nil, the fixed element of a semi-variable overhead item also disappears.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Depreciation under the straight line method, worked out on the original cost of the asset, remains the same in each year of its life.
2. Depreciation under the written down value method decreases from year to year, being worked out on the diminishing book value of the asset.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A shop absorbs on-cost on its jobs as a percentage of material cost. The price of its main material rises steeply, though the work done in the shop and its own indirect expenses are unchanged. Its job costs will:

options.A: Become equal for all jobs, whatever material is used on them
options.B: Fall, because dearer material is used more economically by the shop
options.C: Remain unaffected, since the indirect expenses of the shop are unchanged
options.D: Rise, because the on-cost charged follows the inflated material cost instead of the activity of the shop

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Primary distribution of workshop overheads apportions them to every cost centre of the workshop, production centres and service centres alike.
2. Secondary distribution charges the cost collected at service centres directly to individual jobs, bypassing the production shops served.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Adding the shop on-cost absorbed on a job to its prime cost gives the works cost of the job.
2. Full cost is reached by adding general on-cost and proforma on-cost to the works cost, making the cost of the outturn comparable with trade prices.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a wrong rate of wages is applied in a labour pay sheet, the amount actually payable to the worker is affected and a recovery or a supplementary payment becomes necessary, as the case may be.
2. Where correct wages are booked to a wrong work order, only the distribution of cost among jobs is affected, and not the amount paid to the worker.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Material issued for a specific manufacture job is, by mistake, booked in the on-cost folio of the shop instead of to the work order of the job. Until the booking is corrected:

options.A: The total cost of the workshop as a whole is increased by the error
options.B: The stores depot remains out of pocket for the material issued
options.C: The wages payable to the workers of the shop are reduced
options.D: The job is under-costed and the on-cost of the shop is overstated, so that other jobs of the shop bear a burden not belonging to them

q: In the workshop accounts, the labour, material and on-cost booked on the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock belonging to another railway are accumulated on work orders kept distinct from those of the home railway's own overhaul work, mainly so that:

options.A: The total cost of the overhaul can be recovered from the owning railway and is not merged with the cost of the home railway's own overhaul work
options.B: The workers on the job can be paid at a different rate of wages
options.C: The job can be excluded from the Workshop Outturn Statement
options.D: The material for the job can be drawn without a requisition

q: Mid-Life Rehabilitation of a coach is distinguished from its Periodic Overhaul in that MLR:

options.A: Is a routine overhaul repeated at every overhaul periodicity of the coach
options.B: Is a heavy, once-in-mid-life renewal involving extensive body and corrosion repairs and renewal of fittings, over and above the scope of a normal Periodic Overhaul
options.C: Consists only of washing and examination of the coach
options.D: Is carried out at the coaching depot and never in a workshop

q: A private siding owner gets repairs to his rolling stock executed in a railway workshop. In the workshop accounts, such repairs are accounted for on the footing that:

options.A: Their cost is borne finally by the Railway as a public service
options.B: Their cost is charged to the Periodic Overhaul programme of the home railway
options.C: Their cost is merged with the cost of the Railway's own stock of the same class
options.D: Their cost, together with the charges leviable, is recoverable from the siding owner, the work being treated as work done for an outside party

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under a workshop incentive scheme, bonus is earned only for the time actually worked on covered work.
2. A worker earns bonus also for his periods of leave and recorded idle time, at the same rate as for time worked on jobs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: There is no single uniform periodicity for the Periodic Overhaul of all rolling stock. This is because:

options.A: Each workshop is free to fix its own periodicity for the stock homed to it
options.B: The periodicity is fixed by the stores depot for each class of stock
options.C: Periodicity is prescribed separately for different classes of stock with reference to their type, construction and utilisation in service
options.D: Stock is overhauled only when the Workshop Accounts Officer so directs

q: A manufacture job executed for an outside party on a deposit-work basis is ready for delivery. Before it is delivered, the workshop accounts ensure that:

options.A: The article is delivered first and its cost is recovered at leisure thereafter

options.C: The cost of the job is written off to shop on-cost
options.D: The party is granted a discount equal to the on-cost of the job

q: A deposit work is completed for a final cost, with charges, lower than the advance deposit taken from the party. The unspent balance of the deposit is:

options.A: Credited to shop on-cost of the workshop

options.C: Adjusted against the final cost, the unspent balance being refunded to the party, any shortfall being recovered before delivery

q: Removing a serviceable component from one unit of rolling stock and fitting it on another unit to keep the latter in service, the donor unit being made good in due course, is known in workshop and depot practice as:

options.A: Reclamation

options.C: Condemnation
options.D: Cannibalisation

q: A workshop bills another accounting unit for work done for it through a transfer certificate or advice. The receiving unit's acceptance of that advice is necessary mainly in order that:

options.C: The stores depot can close its price ledger for the month
options.D: The outturn programme of the receiving unit is increased

q: A job in a workshop is accompanied both by job cards and by operation cards. The operation card differs from the job card in that it:

options.A: Records the attendance of the worker at the workshop gate

options.D: Is the authority under which material is purchased for the job

q:
Consider the following statements:

Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Inspection of an article at an intermediate stage of its manufacture in a workshop, instead of only at the end, serves mainly to:

options.A: Detect defects at an intermediate stage of manufacture itself, so that further work is not wasted on an article already defective
options.B: Replace the final inspection of the finished article altogether
options.C: Fix the wages of the workers engaged on the article
options.D: Price the material issued for the article

q: From a machine utilisation statement maintained in a workshop, one can see, machine-wise or shop-wise:

options.A: The wages paid to the operators of each machine
options.B: The quantity of material consumed on each machine
options.C: The hours for which the machines were available, the hours actually worked and the hours lost with reasons such as breakdown or want of work
options.D: The scrap produced on each machine during the month

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Idle facilities mean the time for which individual workers remain waiting for work or material.

Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: As a function of production control, sequencing of the jobs waiting on a machine or in a shop means:

options.A: Deciding the order in which the waiting jobs will be taken up on the machine, so that machine time is used to the best advantage and urgent jobs are not held up
options.B: Deciding the shops through which a job will pass during manufacture
options.C: Fixing the dates by which the annual programme is to be completed
options.D: Inspecting the jobs in the order of their completion

q:
Consider the following statements:

Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In internal check, it is found that a shop has incurred expenditure on a job, but no work order for the job has been received in the Workshop Accounts Office. The correct course is to:
